messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: smart-routing: sudden rise in 5xx and cross-region hops. Auto-paged to #incidents and oncall. Summary tag: routing-fallback-retry-amplification.

alexa_oncall: seeing a spike in origin->fallback->origin loops. 5xx rate up ~4x across eu-north and us-west. users hitting timeouts and retrying. cluster metrics show repeated reroute events every ~200ms for same request ids. paging in.

raj_eng: digging in. quick tl;dr: policy "policy-xy-402" has two variants with overlapping aliases: "rw-llama-large-eu" and "rw-llama-large-q8". alias resolution returns a list and we pick first match; ordering differs across router instances after a recent migration, so eu traffic sometimes lands on q8 (non-local) and triggers failover back to eu -> bounce.

lee_sre: that explains the repeated hops. customers with aggressive SDK retry settings (0ms, 50ms, 100ms) are amplifying. immediate suggestion: 1) disable cross-region fallback for policy-xy-402 2) enable a server-side reroute cooldown (15s) 3) apply an emergency edge throttle for the route.

raj_eng: agree. i'll prepare a hotfix and a canary. can we toggle fallback quickly?

deploy-bot: POST /api/policies/policy-xy-402/disable_fallback (requested by lee_sre)

incident-bot: action accepted: fallback disabled for policy-xy-402 at 09:12:48 UTC.

tom_support: pushing interim customer notice to affected accounts: "We're investigating elevated errors for inference endpoints. We have applied an emergency routing change and will send updates. If you see degraded performance, please reply here." Sending to billing/high-touch for top 10 impacted.

maria_csm: looping in account teams for fintech-prod-5, analytics-corp. I'll coordinate credits if needed and request logs.

lee_sre: emergency edge throttle applied:
```
# emergency edge throttle
redwood edge set-throttle --route /v1/generate --policy policy-xy-402 --limit 75rps
```

raj_eng: while throttle is up, i'm deploying a small router patch: prefer same-region matches when client region present, and add 15s cooldown per request-id for reroute decisions. will canary at 3% for 10 minutes. also will emit a metric 'reroute_count_per_request' to detect loops.

deploy-bot: started canary rollout for routing-hotfix @ 09:18:10 UTC (3% traffic).

alexa_oncall: monitoring dashboards. retry amplification metric peaked shortly after the incident started; after fallback disable and throttle, amplification ratio dropped ~65% within 30s.

raj_eng: canary metrics look good at 10m. no bounce loops on canary, cross-region hops down to baseline. beginning progressive rollout.

lee_sre: removing emergency throttle in 5 once rollout passes. also pushed a server header for proxies to respect backoff: Retry-After: 6

tom_support: updating customers: "We've applied an emergency routing change and temporary throttles. We expect normal traffic to resume shortly. We'll send a detailed timeline and RCA."

maria_csm: captured impacted request ids and will collate logs for postmortem. scheduling a customer follow-up meeting with engineering.

raj_eng: rollout complete at 09:32:51 UTC. final verdict: root cause = stale alias entries + racey variant ordering across routers introduced by migration + aggressive client retry policies without jitter. fixes deployed: alias precedence by origin region, per-request reroute cooldown (15s), server-side jitter added to reroute flow, migration script to prune stale aliases.

lee_sre: action items before close:
- SRE: add alert for high reroute_count_per_request (>3) and automated mitigation to disable fallback for that policy id
- Eng: add post-migration validation to ensure alias lists are consistent cluster-wide
- Devex: update SDK default retry backoff to include jitter and recommend exponential backoff
- Support/CSM: finalize customer communications and credits

alexa_oncall: handing off oncall to raj_eng for post-incident actions. i'll be OOO in 30m.

incident-bot: oncall transfer: alexa_oncall -> raj_eng at 09:36:02 UTC.

deploy-bot: removed emergency throttle for policy-xy-402 @ 09:37:20 UTC.

tom_support: confirmed customers acknowledged interim note; two accounts requested formal postmortem.

maria_csm: will own the postmortem and publish within 48h. assigned owners: raj_eng (engineering), lee_sre (SRE), devex (SDK docs), tom_support (customer comms).

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (stabilized) at 09:40:01 UTC. severity: SEV-2.

lee_sre: please file a follow-up to harden migration tooling and add a migration-time consistency check. also we'll run a repro test for client retry amplification in staging.

raj_eng: will open a changelist for alias cleanup and add unit tests. thanks team. :thumbsup:

maria_csm: publishing customer-facing summary after internal postmortem.

incident-bot: thread closed.
